ap_computer_science_a-m01.set_intro: Consider the following Shelf class, which keeps track of the items stored on a shelf of limited capacity and the items that did not fit.

options.why: Believes a rejected batch is also added to the stock.
Believes an item batch that does not fit is partly stored, filling the shelf to capacity.
A batch is stored only when it fits within the capacity 12; the stock is 8 and the items of rejected batches total 8. Tracing the code gives 8 8.
Believes the rejected count is the number of rejected batches, not the number of items.

items.stem: The Shelf class needs a method percentFull that returns the whole-number percent of the capacity that is currently filled with stock (for example, 41 when 5 of 12 places are filled). Which of the following implementations works as intended?

options.why: Divides the two ints first, which gives 0 until the shelf is full.
Divides by the rejected count, which is zero when nothing was rejected, causing an ArithmeticException.
The multiplication happens before the integer division, so the whole-number percent is not rounded down to 0.
Computes the percent that is empty, not the percent that is full.
